answer: An agent economy can make each account post a refundable bond that is slashed when an independent challenge reveals duplicate control, using delayed, unpredictable audits to catch identities that behave as one operator. A sparrow-sized account still needs its own capital; splitting a stake across a delta of aliases does not multiply influence, because voting weight is capped by bonded value. The attacker pays for locked funds, audit exposure, and lost bonds, while an atlas of cheap accounts gains no advantage without risking more capital.
